title: Storm-2949 -- Azure management-plane credential harvesting after SSPR-abuse account takeover (2026-05-18)
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Real, actively-tracked cloud-identity campaign disclosed by Microsoft Threat Intelligence on 2026-05-18 (Storm-2949 -- temporary designation, not yet attributed to a named actor), cross-verified against independent secondary write-ups (SC Media, TheCyberExpress, SOCPrime, Specops).

Confirmed by BOTH the primary source and at least one independent source: initial access via abuse of Microsoft Entra ID's Self-Service Password Reset (SSPR) flow -- the actor initiates an SSPR request against a targeted account and social-engineers the victim (posing as internal IT support) into approving the resulting MFA prompt, letting the actor reset the password and strip existing authentication methods, eliminating MFA as a control. The actor then uses the Microsoft Graph API plus custom Python (Azure SDK) scripts to enumerate users, roles, service principals, and applications, searches OneDrive/SharePoint for IT-ops files and VPN configs, and installs ScreenConnect (renamed to resemble a legitimate Windows component per the independent write-ups, exact string not disclosed) for persistent remote access.

This rule targets the credential-harvesting stage, using the exact Azure Resource Manager operation names published directly in Microsoft's own advisory: publishing-profile retrieval (publishxml/action, which returns FTP/WebDeploy cleartext credentials), SQL server firewall-rule creation (opening external database access), and storage-account key listing (listkeys/action, harvesting long-lived access keys). Each is individually a real Azure admin action, so this rule flags on any single occurrence (level: high, not critical) -- true correlation (same caller identity, multiple of these operations, short window) needs a Sigma correlation document, which this corpus's rule format does not yet render; reviewers should cross-check CallerIpAddress/Caller across hits before escalating.

Verification discipline: the exact Defender-disabling PowerShell cmdlets and the exact renamed ScreenConnect service name are described narratively by the sources but no verbatim command/string was published by either -- deliberately left out of this rule's detection logic rather than guessed.
